title: nada más, ver in the past, vez / otra vez, a la vez, possessives (mi, tu, nuestro, su), propio

cards.title: más = else
cards.body: The s and t in comiste both signal informal 'you', which helps you remember the ending.

cards.title: ver: vi, vio, vimos, viste, vieron

examples.en: Didn't you see me last night?

cards.title: la vez = time (occasion)
cards.body: Otra vez = 'other time' (no 'an'), meaning again. Nosotros = nos + otros, 'us others'.

examples.en: I want to see them one more time.
Did you go out dancing again?

cards.title: llegaste / llegó tarde otra vez
cards.body: Here Spanish does use -ing: 'wanting to speak with me'.

examples.en: He came to my house again, wanting to talk to me.
examples.es: Llegó a mi casa otra vez queriendo hablar conmigo.

cards.title: mi, tu; ¿a qué hora?; a la vez
cards.body: Mi casa es tu casa. Todos = everybody (also todo el mundo).

examples.en: What time did they arrive at your house?
examples.es: ¿A qué hora llegaron a tu casa?

examples.en: Everybody arrived at my house at the same time.
examples.es: Todos llegaron a mi casa a la vez.

examples.en: I didn't find anything else in your house.
examples.es: No encontré nada más en tu casa.

cards.title: nuestro = our; agreement
cards.body: Possessives agree with the thing owned: mi → mis; nuestro → nuestra / nuestros / nuestras.

cards.title: su = his / her / their / your (formal)
cards.body: Su(s) agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: their house = su casa; his houses = sus casas.

examples.en: I want to go to his / their house.
I want to go to their houses.
I saw it with my own eyes.
examples.es: Lo vi con mis propios ojos.

examples.en: I want to live in my own house.
examples.es: Quiero vivir en mi propia casa.
